definitions.explanation: A section of tree trunk that has been cut but not yet processed into lumber. Retains its round, natural shape.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}に{丸太|まるた}が{流|なが}れてきた。
examples.english: A log came floating down the river.

examples.japanese: キャンプ{場|じょう}に{丸太|まるた}で{作|つく}ったベンチがあった。
examples.english: There was a bench made from logs at the campground.

notes:
USAGE:
A concrete, everyday noun. Appears in contexts involving forestry, construction, camping, and nature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸太小屋|まるたごや} (log cabin)
- {丸太|まるた}を{切|き}る (to cut logs)
- {丸太|まるた}を{組|く}む (to assemble logs)

WORD FORMATION:
{丸|まる} (round) + {太|た} (thick). Describes the round, thick shape of an uncut tree trunk.
